title: Audit ~106 puzzles for QG rule-2 violations (smuggled + mis-demoed)
description:
Goal: Produce a comprehensive findings drawer cataloging every QG rule-2 violation across the ~106 fully-implemented puzzles. Read-only research bead — no code changes here.

Files (read-only):
- puzzles/*/README.md (lesson + worked example + puzzle text)
- puzzles/*/solution/*.tla (actual constructs used)
- docs/curriculum/*/T??.md, R??.md, J??.md (per-puzzle pages with builds-on chain)
- bd labels (concept tags per puzzle, if present)
- QUALITY_GATE.md (the rule definitions)

Scope: only fully-implemented puzzles (~106). Skip stubs/scaffolds.

Method (per puzzle):
1. Identify the claimed "one new thing" from the lesson section.
2. Extract every TLA+/PlusCal construct used in the solution.
3. Compute should-already-know set = union of constructs introduced by all puzzles in the transitive `builds-on` chain.
4. Smuggled = (constructs in solution) − (claimed new concept) − (should-already-know set).
5. Mis-demoed check — for each construct the lesson claims to introduce: does the worked example demonstrate it canonically and non-gratuitously? Flag self-contradicting demos (e.g., T04's `goto`s that say "use this to divert flow" but mostly go to the next sequential label).
6. Note when a demo deliberately uses a non-idiomatic form for pedagogical purposes — that's allowed IF the lesson annotates it as such, otherwise it's a violation.

Output: one MemPalace drawer in `tla_puzzles/curriculum`, table-shaped:
| puzzle | claimed concept | smuggled[] | mis-demoed[] | severity (low/med/high) | suggested fix shape (extract upstream / new puzzle / inline-explain / annotate-as-demonstrative) |

Steps:
1. Enumerate fully-implemented puzzles (filter the puzzles/ dir, drop stubs).
2. Walk per puzzle through the method above (consider parallel sub-agents per tier).
3. Cross-check T04 entries against existing diagnosis drawer (drawer_tla_puzzles_curriculum_94e328409a3c5ac27ba69d27) — they should agree.
4. File the findings drawer.
5. Add bd notes on this bead linking to the drawer ID.

Acceptance:
- Every fully-implemented puzzle has a row.
- T04 entries match the prior diagnosis drawer (self = smuggled, goto = mis-demoed).
- Findings drawer ID recorded in bd notes on this bead.
- Findings inform the per-fix beads filed afterward (those beads are NOT created here).

title: verify-puzzle.sh: copy helper modules to scratch dir
description: Tier 6 audit (tla-3vt.6) surfaced that verify-puzzle.sh copies only <base>.tla + .cfg to its scratch dir, omitting helper modules (e.g., AbstractCard.tla, Counter.tla, OrderStates.tla, Timer.tla, CounterA.tla, RingCount.tla, AbstractLight.tla, AbstractSignal.tla). When TLC tries to resolve a multi-module spec it errors with 'Cannot find source file for module ...', but the elif chain in verify-puzzle.sh falls through to PASS-OTHER (rc=0 because pcal-rc check passes and the script eventually hits 'Finished in'). Net effect: T51, T52, T54-T59 (and likely Tier 5 specs that are multi-module) are NOT actually verified by the gate — they all currently report PASS-OTHER instead of being rejected. Direct TLC runs in each solution/ dir confirm the puzzles themselves are correct. Two possible fixes: (a) copy the entire solution/ dir to scratch (simplest), or (b) detect cross-module FAIL via 'Cannot find source file' / 'Parsing or semantic analysis failed' patterns.

title: Add forward-reference + data-structure-introduction principles to QUALITY_GATE.md rule 2
description:
Goal: Document the two methodological principles locked during the tla-0w8.1 audit (2026-05-06) so future puzzle authors and audits have a clear standard.

Audit findings: drawer_tla_puzzles_curriculum_45aa23d4d99a54513e81d6d0
Tribal fact: bd remember qg-rule-2-audit-principle-locked-2026-05-06

Principle 1 — Forward-reference allowed for advanced concepts:
A puzzle MAY use an advanced TLA+ construct in passing (check-only forward reference) without violating Gate 2 IF the construct gets formal treatment in a later puzzle. Example: T03 uses <>(...) in its Check section; <> is formally introduced in T42. T03 passes Gate 2 because the forward reference resolves.
Limitation: forward-reference does NOT apply when the construct is required by the puzzle's solution (would be smuggling), only when it appears in checks/asides.

Principle 2 — Strict vs Pragmatic Gate 2 (data-structure introduction = one concept):
- Introduce a NEW data structure with all essential ops (T09 records: constructor+dot+EXCEPT; T10 sequences: literal+Append+Head+Tail+Len) → PASS as ONE concept (pragmatic reading; the structure itself is the concept).
- Add more ops to an EXISTING data structure (T11 \o+SubSeq added to sequences from T10; T22 IF-expr+CASE added to existing expression language) → REVISE — split into two concepts (strict reading).

Touches:
- QUALITY_GATE.md — add principles as clarifications under section 2 (Minimal Novelty); reference the 2026-05-06 audit as source.

Acceptance:
